title: Doaba Settlement and the Maratha Transition

blocks.text: The Dina Beg-Wadbhag Singh episode closes with further payment, praise for the sacred offering, and a final reckoning of the region's revenues. An additional sum is settled, the Doaba assessment is fixed at one and a quarter lakh, and the Khalsa agrees to stop the ransacking of Doaba once these terms are secured.

The page then deliberately pivots into Episode 125, signaling that a new political landscape is opening beyond the immediate Jalandhar settlement. Mughal weakness around Delhi, Ahmad Shah Abdali's Kandahari power, and the rising role of the Marathas and the Khalsa are introduced as connected forces reshaping North India.

Dina Beg again recognizes that major conflict cannot be managed without Sikh participation, so the transition leads directly into new negotiations and campaigns. This hinge page therefore both settles on one and a quarter lakh as the agreement and opens the wider story of Marathas and the Khalsa.
